sources.title: Timely Endocytosis of Cytokinetic Enzymes Prevents Premature Spindle Breakage during Mitotic Exit
sources.supports: Primary live imaging supports coordination of spindle disassembly with centripetal septum deposition and actomyosin ring constriction. Opened publisher full text, introduction and results.

sources.title: Role of actin and Myo2p in polarized secretion and growth of Saccharomyces cerevisiae
sources.supports: Primary perturbation experiments and live microscopy support intracellular actin cables and Myo2-mediated polarized secretion/bud growth. PubMed abstract and figure descriptions opened. PMC117377 full-text retrieval failed and is not claimed as evidence.

findings.evidence: The three visible chromatin tubes are stretched only along x while the nuclear neck narrows radially. At p=.749, 288/1971 actual tube vertices exceed the full underlying nuclear-envelope profile; maximum radial excess is .202961 scene units. The failure is already present at p=.65 (45 vertices) and is not the intentional front cutaway.
findings.whyWrong: The persistent chromosome/chromatin representation crosses out of an envelope explicitly described as intact closed mitosis. DNA bead fitting does not constrain the separate detailed chromatin tubes.
findings.fix: Drive detailed chromatin through the same inherited nuclear compartments and constrict/partition the tubes continuously with the nuclear shape, keeping visible DNA inside the persistent envelope and retaining detail.
findings.verification: Measure actual chromatin tube vertices against actual envelope cross sections over .60-.76, including irregular seeks and the daughter handoff; assert containment with margin and inheritance rather than checking only DNA beads.

findings.evidence: Cables are fixed curves extending to local x=1.4 and y=+/-.45; update changes only x scale. At p=.2, 112/1170 cable vertices are outside the underlying cell envelope (max radial excess .29915). At p=.12001 the cable ends extend beyond the small bud axial bound.
findings.whyWrong: Actin cables supporting polarized intracellular transport must remain within the connected mother-bud cytoplasm; the visible early cable runs into extracellular space rather than following the expanding bud.
findings.fix: Deform the preallocated cable geometry to the actual mother/neck/bud path and constrain both radius and length to growth; keep visible secretion carriers consistent with that intracellular route.
findings.verification: Sample all rendered cable vertices through early growth, especially .12-.30, against actual mother and daughter plasma-membrane profiles; verify smooth growth and finite/stable geometry inventories.

limits: Read full piecewise timeline; ran targeted boundary diagnostics and existing smoke. No browser playback or physical-display frame cadence measured.

limitations: Chromosome counts and timing are schematic. Nuclear replacement at p=.75 and onset of cytoplasmic anatomy still require rendered visual review after containment corrections.
No browser review, full-workspace tests, performance benchmark, commit or deployment performed. Phase A product and tests are unchanged.

sources.title: The intramolecular 13C-distribution in ethanol reveals the influence of the CO2-fixation pathway and environmental conditions on the site-specific 13C variation in glucose
sources.supports: Primary 13C measurements and Table 1 support glucose C1/C6 becoming ethanol methyl carbon and C2/C5 becoming methylene carbon; the paper explicitly assigns CO2 to C3/C4. Publisher full text and relevant Table 1/paragraphs opened.

sources.title: Nonstatistical 13C distribution during carbon transfer from glucose to ethanol during fermentation is determined by the catabolic pathway exploited
sources.supports: Primary experimental abstract and figure captions identify the EMP route in S. cerevisiae and track glucose-to-ethanol carbon affiliation. PubMed abstract and figures opened; full-text mirror was unavailable.

findings.evidence: The initial chain is object indices 0-1-2-3-4-5. At the final frame indices 0 and 3 become CO2, while ethanol retains pairs 1-2 and 4-5. Thus one terminal glucose carbon becomes CO2 and one central cleavage carbon remains ethanol. This is wrong whichever end of the initial chain is called C1.
findings.whyWrong: EMP fermentation releases original glucose C3/C4 as CO2 and retains C1/C2 and C5/C6 in ethanol. This scene explicitly promises carbon-fate tracking with preserved connectivity; all six atoms surviving is insufficient if the identities take the wrong products.
findings.fix: Reverse the first triose carbon orientation before pyruvate formation, preserving object identity and bond connectivity, so original indices 2 and 3 are decarboxylated and original terminal pairs remain in ethanol.
findings.verification: Track actual six mesh identities from initial chain adjacency to final C-C bonds/CO2 oxygen bonds under both oxygen conditions. Require CO2 identities to equal the two atoms of the initially broken middle bond and retain six unique carbons throughout.

limits: Read full piecewise timeline; ran targeted boundary diagnostics and existing smoke. No browser playback or physical-display frame cadence measured.

limitations: The model omits full atoms, glycolysis intermediates, respiratory branch and quantitative flux. Chemical symbol visibility is an intentional state change; no claim of atomistic reaction kinetics.
No browser review, full-workspace tests, performance benchmark, commit or deployment performed. Phase A product and tests are unchanged.

sources.title: Nuclear fusion during yeast mating occurs by a three-step pathway
sources.supports: Primary electron tomography and live imaging support opposite-type mating, cell fusion before nuclear congression, cytoplasmic SPB-associated microtubules, and nuclear-envelope fusion before SPB fusion. PMC full text opened, paragraphs 104-125 and results.

findings.evidence: At p=.25, visible vesicles cross a modulus boundary and move 1.62060 scene units with radius .06 unchanged. A pheromone wrap at p=(1-6/7)/1.8 moves 1.099998 units with radius .055 unchanged. Both objects are visible immediately before and after the jump.
findings.whyWrong: The fully visible particles teleport across the scene during continuous playback; the issue is an actual finite screen-space trajectory jump, not the existence of a schematic flow loop.
findings.fix: Fade or taper particle size continuously to zero at each path endpoint before recycling and smoothly gate stage activation/deactivation; retain particles and deterministic phase.
findings.verification: Sample both sides of every active modulus boundary in the compatible branch; require opacity/size to tend to zero as the positional reset occurs. Check same-type branch remains inactive.

findings.evidence: The condition opening >= 1 changes the left MT endpoint from x=-.66 at p=.619999 to x=.13 at p=.62, with y=0/z=.53 and fixed .025 radius; the right side mirrors this .79-unit instant elongation.
findings.whyWrong: A cytoplasmic microtubule visibly snaps across the connection when the opening finishes. The current containment assertions sample on either side but do not detect the sudden growth.
findings.fix: Grow the MT tips continuously into the joined cytoplasm after a sufficient opening exists, maintaining containment and the NE anchor at every intermediate position.
findings.verification: Actual MT cylinder endpoints sampled around .62 must have a displacement converging to zero as time step shrinks; retain cell and nucleus containment tests for the entire interpolation.

findings.evidence: For partner=same the labels become a/a and right chromosome beads change to teal, but mating-inherited-chromatin-1 retains rose tubes (#b68190) while the legend still identifies rose as alpha-parent/alpha-factor. Both inherited chromatin groups stay visible.
findings.whyWrong: The negative-control nucleus simultaneously shows a-type beads and alpha-coded inherited chromatin. This is an important mismatch between the condition, object identity and color explanation.
findings.fix: Apply the same selected mating-type identity to every right-parent chromatin material and ensure the same-type state has a consistent legend/labels without removing detail.
findings.verification: Inspect real tube materials in both inherited-chromatin groups through both conditions and repeated toggles; require same a identity in a/a and separate parental colors in compatible mating.

limits: Read full piecewise timeline; ran targeted boundary diagnostics and existing smoke. No browser playback or physical-display frame cadence measured.

limitations: Nuclear-envelope double-bilayer fusion is shown as a coarse topology transition, not the resolved three-step molecular pathway; morphology at p=.77 requires integrator visual review.
No browser review, full-workspace tests, performance benchmark, commit or deployment performed. Phase A product and tests are unchanged.

sources.title: Recruitment of the lipid kinase Mss4 to the meiotic spindle pole promotes prospore membrane formation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
sources.supports: Primary study establishes vesicle fusion on the meiotic outer plaque, an initial prospore membrane anchored to an SPB embedded in nuclear envelope, and maintenance of membrane-SPB attachment. Full-text XML opened through Europe PMC and saved as evidence/yeastLife/PMC10092644.xml.

findings.evidence: MII spindle endpoints remain at z=.02 and y=+/-(.25+1.45*mii)/2. The four visible SPB spheres are fixed at y=+/-.82,z=-.37. Their nearest spindle endpoint gaps are .77287 at p=.52, .45665 at .60, and .39115 at .67/.71, much greater than SPB radius .08. The nascent membrane cup basal pole is z=-.64, a further .27 from the SPB center.
findings.whyWrong: The illustrated organizing bodies are detached from the actual spindles and nascent membrane site, obscuring the SPB-based nuclear-envelope/meiotic-outer-plaque origin explicitly described by the scene.
findings.fix: Derive spindle endpoints, SPB surface anchors and nascent prospore membrane origin from one consistent changing nuclear geometry; retain four eventual nuclei, membrane growth and ordered wall deposition.
findings.verification: Assert actual MII cylinder endpoints meet SPB geometry and actual SPB sites are anchored at the common NE surface throughout MII; assert the initial PSM nucleation site adjoins the outer plaque before growth. Use triangle-surface or analytically exact surface constraints, not nearest arbitrary vertices.

findings.evidence: At p=2/3 the active vesicle with index 8 resets its modulo parameter from almost 1 to 0, jumping .838151 scene units while remaining visible with radius .047. Additional wraps occur across q=.59-.82.
findings.whyWrong: Secretory vesicles visibly teleport from the growing membrane back into cytoplasm during playback instead of undergoing an unobtrusive replenishment transition.
findings.fix: Taper/fade vesicles at departure/delivery and their global active interval, retaining continuous transport and the current node inventory.
findings.verification: Check every active modulo boundary and .59/.82 activation edges under starved conditions for vanishing visible extent at reset; rich condition remains inactive and arbitrary seeks deterministic.

limits: Read full piecewise timeline; ran targeted boundary diagnostics and existing smoke. No browser playback or physical-display frame cadence measured.

limitations: Recombination is a stated color-exchange schematic; it is not a molecular trajectory. Common-envelope handoff at p=.8 and sequential opaque wall appearance require rendered review; no claim of smoothness acceptance based solely on metadata or unit tests.
No browser review, full-workspace tests, performance benchmark, commit or deployment performed. Phase A product and tests are unchanged.
